vulnerabilities.description: NEW, and the same defect class the commit set out to close, left standing in the sibling field. tools/eap.ts:931 reports `degraded: progress?.degradedClaims ?? []` — the LAST batch's degradations only — on the NON-REPLAY branch, which is the only branch that is not a replay and therefore the one a caller reads to learn what a recall invalidated. Reproduced on 7b497fa: closure k1<-k2<-k3<-k4, cognitive.recall with batchSize:1 returned {complete:true, status:'completed', affectedClaimIds:['k1','k2','k3','k4'], degradedClaims:[{claimId:'k4',...}]} — one of four. Replaying the SAME case immediately after returned degradedClaims with all four, so the two branches of recallOutcome disagree about the same durable case. The commit correctly diagnosed last-batch-only emission for TruthOwnershipSuspended and moved it into the projection; the identical last-batch-only truncation in the degradation report was not moved with it. Durable state is correct (candidates and recall_cases.state hold all four); only the client-facing summary under-reports. Default batchSize is the whole closure, so this is invisible unless the caller batches — which is exactly what an operator does on a large closure.

NEW, introduced by the gate. REHAB_WITHOUT_PROOF carries obligation 'percorrer o caminho normal de verificação', but no code path lets a candidate walk that path: findRecallClosureMembership (eap/recall-closure.ts:43) matches on membership in `recall_cases.closure` alone, nothing ever removes a claim from a closure or retires a case, and the gate is checked on both VERIFY (tools/eap.ts:313) and every promoted candidate (tools/eap.ts:491). Reproduced: after recall of k1, `cognitive.propose VERIFY k2 evidence:['fresh-proof-new']` is refused REHAB_WITHOUT_PROOF; new evidence changes nothing because evidence is not an input to the gate. The refusal names a remedy the system does not implement. Two consequences make it reachable rather than theoretical. (1) CROSS-USER: `register` puts every user in tenant 'default'; user 'mallory' contested alice's claim k1 with severity 'invalidating' and evidence ['x'], recalled it, and permanently froze VERIFY and promotion for alice's whole reverse-dependency closure, tenant-wide across every horizon — no operator, admin or ADR-free path reverses it. Contest-by-any-tenant-member is pre-existing and spec'd; what is new is that its effect is now irreversible and extends to indirect dependents. (2) COMPOUNDED BY THE DISCLOSED PARTIAL: a batch-cap-exhausted recall cannot be resumed by tool, so its closure stays frozen forever with no path to completion — reproduced with RECALL_LIMITS.maxBatches=1, where k3 (never processed, status 'checkpointed') is already refused REHAB_WITHOUT_PROOF and the retry replays the partial case. Held at MEDIUM, not HIGH, deliberately: the gate fails CLOSED, the domain genuinely recorded these claims as resting on a retracted premise, and 003 §Explicitly Deferred Decisions defers the destination status this dead end resolves into. This is the deferred ADR coming due, not a coding error — but the obligation string should not promise a path that does not exist.

NEW. findRecallClosureMembership (eap/recall-closure.ts:48) does an UNINDEXED full-table scan of `recall_cases` and JSON.parses every closure blob on EVERY VERIFY and once PER CANDIDATE inside eapPromoteGoverned's loop — which runs inside a serialTransaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), so it holds the tenant's write lock for the duration. `recall_cases` is append-only and unbounded, and any tenant member can grow it cheaply (one contest + one recall per row). Measured on 7b497fa: 2000 cases x 50 closure ids gave ~13ms per lookup (258ms / 20 lookups), linear in rows x closure size. A 50-candidate promotion at that table size is ~650ms of serialized write lock; at 20k cases it is tens of seconds. No failure reproduced — recorded as a scalability defect on a newly-hot path, not an exploit.

NEW, low reach, and the fail-closed direction. A SINGLE unparseable `recall_cases.closure` row halts the lifecycle for the ENTIRE tenant: the scan raises StoredStateCorruptionError on the first bad row it meets, so every VERIFY and every promotion — including candidates with no relationship to any recall — is refused RESOURCE_ABSENT naming an unrelated case id. Reproduced: inserted a single row rc-bad with closure='{not json' and an otherwise clean candidate u1 was refused at VERIFY with "Stored recall_cases.closure for 'rc-bad' is not readable JSON". The refusal is typed and no stack trace escapes (the new eapPropose wrapper works), and failing open here would defeat the gate, so the direction is right. What is missing is any repair or quarantine path: one corrupt row, reachable through direct column corruption or a rebuildFromJsonl replay of a foreign-schema mirror, is an unrecoverable tenant-wide outage.

edgeCasesMissed: RE-VERIFIED FIXED BY REPRODUCTION, not by claim. (1) The PRIMARY gap is CLOSED. Exact prior reproduction re-run on 7b497fa: k2.refs=['k1'], contest+recall k1 -> affectedClaimIds ['k1','k2'], k1='recalled' and k2 still 'admitted' (the deferral holds, no status invented); CONCRETIZE k2 -> ok:true; VERIFY k2 -> REHAB_WITHOUT_PROOF; promote k2 -> refused with 0 rows in `proposals` and 0 candidates in root. (2) All five advertised inputSchemas match their handlers: every cognitive.* tool called with EXACTLY its advertised `required` list succeeded — propose(token,horizonId,candidateId,command,evidence) ok, promote(token,childHorizonId,targetParentHorizonId,candidateIds) minted a promotionId, contest and recall ok, and basedOnSeq is now advertised on propose and promote with real bounds. (3) weird-state is CLOSED: ILLEGAL_TRANSITION 'holds unrecognized lifecycle state' and the row still reads 'weird-state' afterwards — untouched, not reset. (4) `checkpoint` is CLOSED: MALFORMED_CONTRACT, and `SELECT count(*) FROM recall_cases` = 0 afterwards, so it is refused before any case is opened. (5) basedOnSeq -0 is CLOSED on the only path that can deliver it: a raw JSON body containing the literal -0 is refused MALFORMED_CONTRACT (note JSON.stringify(-0) emits '0', so an SDK client cannot even send it). (6) The TL's event finding is CLOSED with no double emission: a 3-cell closure driven at batchSize:1 produced exactly 3 TruthOwnershipSuspended events, one per cell INCLUDING the cells suspended in non-final batches, all 3 cells 'suspended' in `authority` with last_flip_by 'recall:<caseId>'; the final batch's checkpoint-then-complete pair projects twice but the already-suspended skip means the second announces nothing, and an immediate replay of the whole recall added 0 further events. RecallWorker.emit is a bounded in-memory debug ring, not the broadcast channel, so it is not a second emitter.

GATE BYPASS HUNT — no bypass found. Probed and refused: promotion of a candidate that reached 'verified' BEFORE the recall; a mixed promotion batch ['k3','k2'] where only k2 is in the closure (the WHOLE contract is refused, no partial distillation, and the clean k3 promotes fine on its own afterwards); the idempotency replay path (an IDENTICAL re-promotion of a legitimately promoted candidate is refused after a later recall rather than replaying — the gate sits ahead of the replay short-circuit, fail-closed, and the original promotion row is untouched); climbing the promoted copy in the PARENT horizon (root DELIBERATE/ADMIT/CONCRETIZE all ok, root VERIFY refused REHAB_WITHOUT_PROOF, so the parent copy cannot reach a grandparent either); and a claim in an ACTIVE, incomplete case (closure is written in full at createSync, so there is no active-case window). The gate matches by claimId tenant-wide across all horizons, which also blocked a freshly created, structurally unrelated candidate in horizon h9 that merely reused the id 'k2' — correct given claim ids are a tenant-global namespace that cognitive.contest already resolves across horizons, but worth an ADR sentence.

003-deferred and NOT re-scored, re-confirmed present: tool-driven resumption of a batch-cap-exhausted recall (disclosed PARTIAL by the implementer; exhaustion IS now truthfully reported via complete:false / remainingClaimIds / batchLimitReached / maxBatches / obligation, and the retry honestly reports the partial case as replayed:true rather than pretending to continue). Its interaction with the new gate is scored above under the MEDIUM MISSING_CONTROL, since together they make the freeze permanent.

Test-scenarios 1.1 'Should escalate without promotion when the Horizon budget is exhausted': still no implementation (budget_allocated written, budget_consumed never incremented or compared). Explicitly deferred by the orchestrator for this round and NOT deducted, recorded only so the gap is not lost.

Test-scenarios 1.1 Horizon 'Should retain horizon-local authority when assignment to another Horizon is attempted': still no explicit refusal path; the invariant continues to hold by construction (a promoted candidate enters the parent at 'proposed', re-verified again this round). Deferred, not deducted.

Carried LOW, deferred as a spec decision and not re-deducted: an Operator Approval is bound to scope/expiry/provenance/basedOnSeq but not to a capabilityId, so a grant issued for one scope executes any capability that declares that targetScope.
